newsitem.title: USA: First Union gains reflect revenue growth.
newsitem.headline: First Union gains reflect revenue growth.

text.p: First Union Corp said Thursday its record earnings of $485 million in the three months ended June 30 reflected growth in revenue combined with expense control.

"Fee income growth continued to be strong in the second quarter, with 148 percent growth from last year in our capital markets group and 51 percent growth from last year in our capital management group," Chairman and Chief Executive Edward Crutchfield said in a statement. "With the economy continuing to show strength, we expect to maintain our momentum throughout this year."

First Union said average net loans increased six percent to $95.3 billion in the second quarter of 1997 compared with $89.8 billion in the second quarter of 1996. Loan growth came primarily from First Union's Capital Markets Group and consumer lending.

Nonperforming assets were $708 million, or 0.73 percent of net loans and foreclosed properties at June 30, 1997, compared with $836 million, or 0.91 percent of net loans and foreclosed properties, at June 30, 1996. Annualized net charge-offs were 0.68 percent in the second quarter of 1997 compared with 0.45 percentin the second quarter of 1996. Net charge-offs, excluding credit card-related charge-offs, were 0.23 percent in the second quarter of 1997 compared with 0.17 percent in the second quarter of 1996.

Per-share earnings in the second-quarter rose 13 percent to $0.87 from $0.77 in the same period a year ago. The per-share figures reflect a two-for-one stock split payable on July 31 to stockholders of record July 1. Before the split, the per-share earnings were $1.73 versus $1.55 a year ago.
